English:
Benefit of community-based SARS-CoV-2 testing for surveillance in Lusaka district, Zambia with emphasis on vulnerable populations: a research and disease management intervention.
Background
Zambia has had 11,512 confirmed COVID-19 cases and 259 deaths as of 20th August 2020. The Lusaka District has been the epicentre of the pandemic in Zambia with 5,348 cases and 136 deaths as of 20th August 2020. The Lusaka City Health Department (LCHD) has been conducting COVID-19 testing and management since February 2020. The LCHD has a well-established health system with multiple clinics and hospitals that provide both primary and secondary health care. The LCHD has been conducting active case and contact tracing, isolating and supporting patients in isolation and quarantine sites, and referring severe cases to the main hospital—Main Public Health Laboratory Institute (MPHLI). The LCHD has also been conducting community mobilization and engagement activities to raise awareness and promote social distancing and hygiene. Despite these efforts, the Lusaka District continues to be the epicentre of the pandemic in Zambia. This could be, in part, due to the Lusaka District’s population density, which is more than six times that of the rest of Zambia. Another possible reason is that the Lusaka District is the economic hub of Zambia and a major transportation route into Zambia from bordering countries. This makes it difficult to control the entry of COVID-19 cases into the District. The LCHD also identified a need to expand testing beyond their current focus on selected facilities to include testing of individuals in the community, especially in high-density areas and among vulnerable populations. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the impact of community-based active case and contact tracing, testing, and isolation on the transmission of SARS-CoV-2 in the Lusaka District.
Methods
This study will be conducted in the Lusaka District of Zambia as a research and disease management intervention. The study population will be a convenience sample of all individuals found to be positive for SARS-CoV-2 by the LCHD from the 7th of July 2020 to the 17th of August 2020. All individuals found to be positive for SARS-CoV-2 will be included in the study.
